describes: Exception cues (exception_ in deontic.ebnf, a sibling constituent of modal_frame, never nested inside it) and the content markers that classify the exception clause once found. 'in accordance with Article N' and similar cross-references are deliberately NOT resolved (no resolver is built): xref_markers and external_terms only classify the clause as one of EXCEPTION_XREF_UNRESOLVED / EXCEPTION_EXTERNAL_UNRESOLVED / internal_parsed, matched by simple membership over the exception clause's words, never by a compiled pattern. NOT an exception lead, and not modelled as anything else: 'by way of derogation from' (EN) / 'abweichend von' (DE). 'By way of derogation from Article 5, R' means R OVERRIDES Article 5 — the CURRENT rule is the exception to the referenced provision, which is the opposite direction of this plane's `exception` slot (a carve-out TO the current rule, stated by the current rule itself, e.g. 'R unless [X]'). Modelling it as an exception lead would invert the relation ('shall not ... by way of derogation from Article 5' would publish exception 'Article 5', reading as 'forbidden unless Article 5' — backwards). It is also not modelled as a condition or a cross-reference; a derogation clause is left wherever the rest of the grammar's existing productions already put it (inside `action`) rather than guess a structure for it. 'abweichend von' is additionally inert in this English-only (Phase 1 scope) prose grammar regardless: no German modal lexeme exists in modal_lexemes.json, so a German sentence never reaches a modal match and always abstains NO_MODAL before any exception lead is even scanned.
